title: Casper and the Confession
premise: August Pemberton, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with an unbroken record of closing cases, recognizes the dead man's clothes as their own — stolen from the closet of the apartment they've kept since childhood. The victim is Danny Voss, who thirty years ago testified against August's foster father in a trial that shattered their found family, and whose alibi that night was woven with August's own. As August retraces the old lies, they discover Danny was preparing to recant his testimony, and that someone in their surviving foster family killed him to keep the confession buried. In the end, August must choose between protecting the only family they have left and delivering the truth to court, and they choose truth — testifying themselves about the night everything went wrong.
about_author: Jonah Vane spent a decade working overnight dispatch jobs in three cities, collecting the voices of strangers at 3 a.m. before turning them into fiction. They write mysteries about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Clothes You Left Behind
chapters.summary: August's POV. Called out at dawn to identify a body found near the depot, August freezes: the victim wears August's own jacket and shirt, taken from their apartment. Detective Ilsa Reyes suspects August first; the clothes are the only evidence linking anyone. Flashbacks surface of the 1994 trial that broke apart August's foster home. Emotional beat: dread and violation — the past has literally dressed itself in August's life.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibi
chapters.summary: August's POV, alternating with recovered journal pages from the victim, Danny Voss. August interviews the scattered survivors of the old foster house — Marisol, now a nurse; Teddy, recently paroled; and quiet Ruthie — mapping who lied about where they stood the night of the original crime. Danny's journal reveals he planned to recant at an upcoming hearing. Emotional beat: uneasy nostalgia curdling into suspicion of everyone August once loved.

chapters.title: What Ruthie Kept
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following Danny's last dispatch call — placed to August's own taxi company — August confronts Ruthie, who admits she drove Danny that night and heard him rehearse his recantation aloud. Ruthie also reveals she saw the killer's car: Teddy's. But when August presses Teddy, he produces proof he was elsewhere, meaning Ruthie lied — or is covering for someone. Emotional beat: betrayal tightening like a noose; the family myth collapses.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: August's POV, climaxing on the eve of the pre-trial hearing. August realizes Marisol orchestrated it all: she silenced Danny to protect Ruthie, who was the true witness to the original crime and would have been destroyed by recantation fallout. Confronted with the journal and the stolen-clothes frame meant to pin Danny's death on August, Marisol confesses. August testifies anyway, ending the thirty-year silence. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve — truth costs the family, but saves August.
